problem.title: First and Last Swipe Per Card
problem.prompt: You are analyzing debit card transaction patterns for a neobank. For each card, you need to identify the merchant of the very first swipe and the merchant of the very last swipe to understand customer journey endpoints. Write a query that returns one row per card showing: `card_id`, `first_merchant` (merchant of earliest transaction by timestamp), and `last_merchant` (merchant of latest transaction by timestamp). Order results by `card_id` ascending. Note: Some cards may have only one transaction, in which case the first and last merchant will be identical.
problem.schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE card_swipes (
  swipe_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  card_id VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  merchant_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  swipe_amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  swipe_timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL
);

composite_moves: window: FIRST_VALUE(merchant_name) OVER (PARTITION BY card_id ORDER BY swipe_timestamp ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
window: LAST_VALUE(merchant_name) OVER (PARTITION BY card_id ORDER BY swipe_timestamp ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
DISTINCT to collapse per-card rows to one row per card_id

hints: You'll need to use window functions to access the first and last values within each card's partition.
FIRST_VALUE works as expected with default frames, but LAST_VALUE requires an explicit frame specification to avoid returning the current row's value.

Use FIRST_VALUE(merchant_name) OVER (PARTITION BY card_id ORDER BY swipe_timestamp) and LAST_VALUE(merchant_name) OVER (PARTITION BY card_id ORDER BY swipe_timestamp ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING), then SELECT DISTINCT to get one row per card.
problem.answer_key:
SELECT DISTINCT
  card_id,
  FIRST_VALUE(merchant_name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY card_id 
    ORDER BY swipe_timestamp 
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  ) AS first_merchant,
  LAST_VALUE(merchant_name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY card_id 
    ORDER BY swipe_timestamp 
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  ) AS last_merchant
FROM card_swipes
ORDER BY card_id;

_meta.scenario: a neobank tracking debit card swipes and deposit funnel

user_solution:
/*
First and Last Swipe Per Card
- For each card identify the very first swipe and  very last swipe to understand customer journey endpoints.
Write a query that returns one row per card showing: `card_id`, `first_merchant` (merchant of earliest transaction by timestamp), and `last_merchant` (merchant of latest transaction by timestamp).
Order results by `card_id` ascending.
Note: Some cards may have only one transaction, in which case the first and last merchant will be identical.

 */
SELECT
    DISTINCT
    card_id,
    FIRST_VALUE(merchant_name) OVER (PARTITION BY card_id ORDER BY swipe_timestamp
                                     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS first_merchant,
    LAST_VALUE(merchant_name) OVER (PARTITION BY card_id ORDER BY swipe_timestamp
                                     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_merchant
FROM card_swipes
ORDER BY 1;
